summary: Registry listing for a Loch Erne fire tower near Thunder Bay, Ontario; one undated description calls it abandoned, with no build or staffing details.

evidence.supports: location given as Thunder Bay, Ontario
a road cleared by the Ministry of Natural Resources
evidence.quote: The road was cleared by the Ministry of Natural Resources

evidence.supports: the road crosses patented claims on the way to the tower
evidence.quote: traverses the patented west-end claims of the Lock Erne group

evidence.supports: the tower is abandoned and lies south of the property
evidence.quote: on route to an abandoned fire tower south of the property

evidence.supports: truck-haulage and rubber-tire tractor roads starting at the Inco road, roughly 4.8 km (three miles) to the east
evidence.quote: Truck haulage and rubber-tire tractor roads leading from the Inco road, some three miles to the east

notes_for_editor: One source, the firelookout.ca entry. Its only substantive text is one undated, unattributed paragraph about access roads, probably from an older mining or exploration report; the page does not say. The paragraph spells the claim group 'Lock Erne' while the registry name is 'Loch Erne'; the story uses the registry name. The registry gives no elevation, tower type, height or year built. The paragraph gives no year for the abandonment, so no events are recorded. The brief's coordinates match the registry. The brief gives no local unit, so the story uses the registry's 'Thunder Bay, ON' only. A search turned up a Facebook post and a YouTube video that name Shebandowan Lake, but neither page rendered its text, so nothing from them is cited.
